Switching from Windows to Mac does not actually impose many software limitations. The platform can run most mainstream computer applications, and there is also a wealth of Mac-exclusive and practical applications to choose from.

The biggest exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that, whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games now run on Mac better than ever before…

Apple has its own proprietary game porting toolkit, which helps developers evaluate how their Windows games run on Mac, aiming to encourage and facilitate game ports to the Mac platform.

However, as Macworld's Filipe Esposito pointed out, this toolkit is also being used by players to run Windows software unofficially on Mac — and he himself is one of them. He noted that the latest test version brings significant performance improvements, using GTA V as an example.

After testing the fourth beta version of the game porting toolkit for several days on a MacBook Pro equipped with the M4 Pro chip, he found that the performance improvements essentially transformed the experience of running demanding Windows games… On the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, using the same game settings and benchmarks, GTA V's frame rate jumped from around 106 fps in the GPTK 3 era to around 176 fps in the GPTK 4 beta, an increase of about 66%. The game ran quite smoothly at 2K resolution with medium-to-high graphics settings.

He acknowledges that not every game will see such a significant boost, but he still hopes these advances will encourage game developers to consider Mac as a viable platform.
